newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas remains centred on prompt, prices steady.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas remains centred on prompt, prices steady.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw a huge volume of trade done on the short term market once again, with trade on the within-day and day-ahead markets once again dominating dealer's interest.
Nearly all the short-term gas done involved the same buyer, who has bought heavily since the beginning of the week.
The company involved remained unwilling to comment directly on the reasons for the surge of interest in the short term.
But a representative of the company has referred to problems at Liverpool Bay, widely assumed to have been at least in part responsible for the recent activity in the short term market.
Further out, the market was comparatively quiet.
There was some good interest in the third quarter, with several trades done in existing ranges between 10.30 pence and 10.325 pence a therm.
Further out there was isolated trade in the October gas year, the first quarter of next year and in summer 1998. Prices were in line with yesterday's levels.
Dealers point out that the trading ranges have now been unchanged for several days, with the lack of volatility deterring traders and limiting spot market activity in many periods.
Some saw the deals done on Tuesday as far forward as the third quarter of 1999 as an attempt to create a new trading period and encourage activity. But this was not seen repeated on Wednesday.
The IPE futures market traded 205 lots, higher than on several days recently although the number of deals was comparatively small, with only 10 separate trades transacted.
But brokers were encouraged by what appeared to be strip trading on the futures contract, rather than deals involving just a single month.
